content: The Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) is regarded as the gold standard for diagnosing Post-Transplantation Diabetes Mellitus (PTDM). This test is typically conducted when the patient has achieved stability on maintenance immunosuppressive therapy, which is generally around 45 days after the transplantation procedure. Screening for PTDM may also involve the use of fasting plasma glucose (FPG) or hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) levels. However, these methods are primarily utilized to identify individuals at high risk of developing PTDM, who may require more intensive monitoring and follow-up. Additionally, pre-transplant levels of high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) have been linked to the development of PTDM in kidney transplant recipients. This suggests that hs-CRP could serve as a potential early biomarker for assessing the risk of PTDM in this patient population.
